review.hazards_note: The underlying concerns are valid, but H1 and H2 prescribe implementations rather than only necessary constraints. H1 should require sufficiently wide, exact arithmetic and safe handling of unbounded endpoints, with signed 64-bit arithmetic as an example rather than a requirement. H2 should prohibit worst-case dense-grid work/storage and require traversal safe on long components; its instruction to store only row/column vertices and known-depth edges excludes P3's legitimate hub and auxiliary edges. H3 and H4 correctly cover global feasibility, the impossible output convention, and isolated coordinates.
